final_message:
**Status:** Reproduced on 9.12.0 only (already fixed). It also reproduces on 9.13.0 and 9.14.0. The checkout given (6f37b07, version 9.15.0) doesn't show the bug.

**Expected:** the fix shouldn't change which `if` the final `else throw ...` belongs to. Either don't fix, or keep the braces.

**Actual (9.12.0 to 9.14.0):** the rule reports `4:9 Unexpected if as the only statement in an else block.` The fix turns `else { if (false) {} }` into `else if (false) {}`. The trailing `else throw ...` then attaches to the new inner `if (false)` instead of the outer `if (true)`. I parsed the fixed output and the outer `if`'s alternate goes from `ThrowStatement` to `null`. Running the code shows the same change: the input doesn't throw, the fixed output does.

**On this checkout:** there's no report and no fix, so the output is unchanged and the script passes. When there's no outer `else`, the rule still fixes the same inner block (`if (true) if (false) {} else { if (false) {} }` becomes `... else if (false) {}`). So it only skips when removing the braces would be unsafe. I compared the published 9.12.0 rule file with the checkout's. The checkout's report condition has an added `!astUtils.areBracesNecessary(parent, sourceCode)` check, and that check catches this dangling-else case.

**Trigger:** an `else { if (...) ... }` with no `else` of its own, belonging to an `if` that is the brace-less consequent of an outer `if ... else`.

**Run:** `node repro/no-lonely-if-dangling-else.js` (this checkout: passes, exit 0). Set `ESLINT_DIR` to an installed ESLint to test another version. For example, after `npm i eslint@9.12.0` in `~/eslint-9.12`, run `ESLINT_DIR=~/eslint-9.12/node_modules/eslint node repro/no-lonely-if-dangling-else.js` (fails, exit 1, with the output above). The CLI on 9.12.0 gives the same broken output (`--rule '{"no-lonely-if":"error"}' --fix-dry-run --stdin`).

**Reliability:** deterministic.

**Artifacts:** `repro/no-lonely-if-dangling-else.js`. It uses the reporter's exact snippet and compares parse and runtime behaviour before and after the fix.

I didn't change any production code. To look into the cause, use 9.12.0 to 9.14.0, since this checkout already contains the fix.
